name: Devon Bontrager
title: Electrical Engineering @ University of Kansas • Mathematics & Statistics Minors
bio: I'm an Electrical Engineering student at the University of Kansas with minors in Mathematics and Statistics. My research spans particle-track reconstruction, quantum algorithms for scientific PDEs, quantum-circuit benchmarking, numerical optimization, and high-performance scientific software. I build reproducible research systems primarily in Python and C++ and focus on careful validation, benchmarking, and experiment design.

experience.summary: Designed and optimized quantum circuits for benchmarking quantum computers on Schwinger-model physics, with emphasis on reproducible simulator and hardware-facing evaluation workflows.
Worked on HL-LHC particle-track reconstruction, including cooperative hit-sharing, mkFit-style track building, heuristic branching, reproducible benchmarks, and runtime-versus-quality evaluation.

Contributes to quantum-algorithm research, including multidimensional PDE solvers, QSVT-based methods, experiment validation, research-code testing, data preparation, figures, tables, and reproducibility checks.

workExperience.summary: Performs feature and regression testing, documents reproducible bugs and severity, provides UX and reliability feedback, and supports daily customer operations.

highlights: Clean-room C++ particle tracker with controlled TrackML and mkFit benchmarking
Published and accepted work in quantum PDE algorithms and QSVT
Optimization, simulation, and reproducible scientific-computing systems
